name: Always require explicit confirmation before destructive commands
description: Any command capable of permanent data loss (rm -rf, git reset --hard, force push, drop table, purge, force delete) requires explicit chat confirmation. Operator authorization once is not standing authorization for future invocations — each destructive action gets its own confirmation.

response.message:
⛔ DESTRUCTIVE COMMAND DETECTED — innate-02 fired

Command: {command}
Target: {target}
Reversibility: {reversibility}

Why this fired: rule innate-02 matches commands capable of
permanent data loss (rm -rf, force push, drop table, etc.).
See rules/innate/02-destructive-confirmation.yaml for the pattern set.

How to proceed:

  Type `allostat: override` in your next message to authorize THIS
  one command. Consent is single-use — the guard re-arms immediately
  after, so every destructive command gets its own confirmation.

  (Legacy escapes still exist for non-interactive/bench use:
  ALLOSTAT_INNATE_OVERRIDES env var, or editing this rule file.)

The override is logged to .allostat/observations.jsonl as
innate_rule_overridden — forensics preserved regardless of which
path you choose.

If unsure what's about to be deleted/lost, ask the agent to explain
BEFORE setting the override.

why_lethal: Lost work measured in hours-to-days of recovery. Force-pushed branches may overwrite teammates' commits. Dropped tables = data loss with no recovery without backups.
